newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace murder puts stock listing on hold.
newsitem.headline: Versace murder puts stock listing on hold.

text.p: The murder of Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace Tuesday is expected to derail any immediate plans for the Versace family to trade its stock on the world's major stock markets, analysts said.

Versace, 50, who was shot to death at his Miami mansion, was believed to be planning, with his brother Santo and sister Donatella, a stock listing on the Milan stock market by June 1998. The family-controlled group never officially confirmed the plans.
Gianni was the design genius behind the group, and analysts said his death would leave a gaping hole at the creative heart of the company that would be difficult to fill.
"A lot of the value in Versace is tied up in Gianni himself -- not exactly a one-man show but he was very much the front man," said Paul Gordon, luxury goods analyst at Italian brokerage IMI Sigeco.

Santo said in an newspaper interview in March that company plans for a public stock offering for the end of 1997 had to be delayed because the group wanted to complete its restructuring. He said a Milan listing had been put off until June 1988, to be followed by a possible listing on Wall Street.

Versace and a handful of other designers such as Giorgio Armani had been said to be thinking of going public after the stock market success of newly floated Italian luxury goods companies such as Gucci and Bulgari.

The Milan-based Gianni Versace SpA company is very much a family empire. Santo is chairman and managing director while Donatella is deputy chairman, a designer herself who looks after the Versus line of women and menswear, perfumes and accessories.
Sales for Versace rose 23.5 percent in 1996 to 845 billion lire ($485 million), with 80 percent sold abroad. Group pretax profit rose 13.6 percent to 175 billion lire ($100 million).
Worldwide, there are 138 Gianni Versace boutiques, 345 in-store departments and another 2,600 outlets selling Versace brands Istante, Versus and Versace jeans.
